candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest classifies this binary as malware with probability 0.985, and all 20 top n-grams push toward cryptojacking (SHAP +0.0079 to +0.0164). However, the n-grams themselves are generic. The highest-frequency ones (MOV PUSH 0.0764, CALL PUSH 0.0695, PUSH CALL 0.0650, POP PUSH 0.0145, XOR PUSH 0.0142, LEA PUSH 0.0113, ADD PUSH 0.0076) reflect ordinary stack-based argument passing and call sequences, which appear in almost any compiled x86 program. No n-gram shows the tight arithmetic or bitwise loops (rotates, shifts, wide XOR/ADD chains) that would point to a hashing or mining kernel. The evidence also lists no functions where the n-grams occur, so none can be tied to a specific routine. Many of the top-ranked n-grams are very rare (POP SUB 0.000073, CDQ MOV 0.000073, MOVZX PUSH 0.000291, SBB INC 0.000218, POP XOR 0.000436, DEC PUSH 0.000436). Their large SHAP values likely reflect the model's learned association with specific compiler or packer styles rather than demonstrable mining behavior. CMOVZ MOV and XOR CALL have frequency 0.000000 yet contribute +0.0099 and +0.0090, so their absence is itself pushing the score toward malware, which is not interpretable as a behavior. The cumulative SHAP weight and the model's high probability support suspicion, but the evidence cannot confirm cryptojacking specifically, so the finding is inconclusive.
